description: Four-operator FM percussion voice; every knob and CV is read at the instant a trigger arrives and held for the whole hit

params.text: Sets the pitch the hit starts at, 1V per octave over four octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Shifts the starting pitch by up to a fifth of a volt either way, about two semitones
Sets the pitch the hit sweeps to, 1V per octave over four octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Picks one of 32 sets of frequency ratios for the four operators
Picks one of 64 combinations of wavetables for the four operators
Picks one of six FM algorithms, setting which operators modulate which and which ones reach the output
Feeds operator 1 back into its own wavetable position, none of it at the bottom of its travel and all of it at the top
Sets how long operators 1 and 3 take to fade out after a trigger, 1ms at the bottom of its travel and doubling with every five per cent of the way up
Sets how long operators 2 and 4 take to fade out after a trigger, 1ms at the bottom of its travel and doubling with every five per cent of the way up
Sets how fast the pitch sweeps from the start pitch to the end pitch; below a fifth of its travel there is no sweep and the pitch stays where it starts
Attenuates and inverts the CV for the release of operators 2 and 4
Attenuates and inverts the CV for the wave combination
Attenuates and inverts the CV for the FM ratios

inputs.text: Adds to the starting pitch at 1V per octave, with the total clamped to four octaves either side of C4
Adds to the end pitch at 1V per octave, with the total clamped to four octaves either side of C4
Steps through the 32 ratio sets, one set per volt with its attenuverter fully up
Steps through the 64 wave combinations, one combination per volt with its attenuverter fully up
Steps through the six algorithms, one algorithm per volt
Adds to the feedback on operator 1, a fifth of the knob's range per volt
Adds to the release of operators 1 and 3, a fifth of the knob's range per volt
Adds to the release of operators 2 and 4 through its attenuverter, a fifth of the knob's range per volt at full
Adds to the pitch envelope speed, a fifth of the knob's range per volt
A rising edge fires the voice and freezes every knob and CV reading for that hit; it reads high above 2V and low below 0.4V
A trigger arriving on the same sample as the main trigger makes that hit louder and its modulation deeper
A rising edge silences the voice at once, dropping both amplitude envelopes to 0V

outputs.text: The voice, reaching about 3.5V, or about 6.3V on an accented hit

notes: The voice is silent until a rising edge reaches Trig: both amplitude envelopes rest at 0V, and every knob and CV is read at that instant and held for the whole hit.
menu: DC Filter — removes any DC offset from the output; it is ticked until it is turned off
Speed Ramp Looping — repeats the pitch envelope instead of running it once per trigger
Trigger mods index — scales the depth of the FM by the height of the trigger voltage
Operators sync on trigger — resets the phase of all four operators on every trigger
